source_review.scope: Five Rust compiler/emitter source files, all three package manifests, workspace/lock/toolchain files, and native/syntax test sources.
findings: Direct source lexing/checking feeds an in-process AST-to-x86-64 emitter, branch patcher and ELF writer.

No process-spawning API, foreign compiler/linker delegation, FFI import, embedded interpreter, opaque compiler seed inclusion or external code generator was found in these compiler crates. std::process::ExitCode supplies CLI status only.
Native print/error routines and instruction bytes are reviewable generator source; they are not an embedded compiler executable.
Zero external Cargo dependencies does not remove Rust standard library, host linker/SDK or operating-system dependencies.
source_review.method: Read source/manifests; inspect Cargo metadata/tree; use source search as a secondary check; inspect PE imports and ELF headers.
source_review.limit: Static review and binary headers are scoped observations, not execution traces proving all possible behavior.

I0.observation: Reviewed source/test paths require no Python; no execution on a Python-absent environment was performed.

I1.observation: Existing unsigned Windows debug seed only; no clean-host standalone distribution proof.

I3.observation: Bounded Rust-based direct ELF emission is observed without interpreter/dynamic imports. The mandatory NAJA-native autonomous backend/linker closure remains future work.

I4.observation: Seed/source/debug hashes inventoried; no B1/B2/B3 fixed point or release reproducibility proof.
